name: Use only approved words, technical nouns, and technical verbs
description: Use only words that are in the STE dictionary. If a word is not in the dictionary, use it only as a technical noun or technical verb. Do not use words that are not approved and are not technical nouns or technical verbs.
specText: Use approved words. If a word is not approved, use it only as a technical noun or a technical verb.

compliantExamples.text: The word 'use' is an approved verb in the dictionary.
The word 'engine' is a technical noun.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Utilize the correct tool.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Utilize' is not an approved word; use 'Use'.

name: Use approved words only as their specified part of speech
description: Each word in the STE dictionary has a specified part of speech (noun, verb, adjective, etc.). Use the word only in that role. Do not use a noun as a verb, or an adjective as a noun, for example.
specText: Use each approved word only as the part of speech that is given in the dictionary.

compliantExamples.text: Test B is an alternative to test A.
Do the leak test of the system.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Test the system for leaks.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Test' is approved as a noun, not a verb in this context.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Dim the lights.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Dim' is an approved adjective but not an approved verb.

name: Use approved words only with their approved meanings
description: The STE dictionary lists which meanings are approved for each word. Use a word only with those approved meanings; do not use a word with a meaning that is not listed in the dictionary.
specText: Use each approved word only with the meaning given in the dictionary.

compliantExamples.text: Do the procedures that follow.
Obey the safety instructions.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Assure that the pressure is correct.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Assure' means to tell a person not to worry; it requires a person as the object. Use 'Ensure' or 'Make sure that' when referring to a condition or fact.

name: Use only approved forms of verbs and adjectives
description: For each approved verb or adjective, the dictionary lists which forms are allowed (e.g. infinitive, imperative, simple past). Do not use forms that are not listed, such as the present perfect or progressive.
specText: Use only the forms of verbs and adjectives that the dictionary permits.

compliantExamples.text: (To) Remove / Remove / Remove(s) / Removed / Removed (past participle as adjective)

nonCompliantExamples.text: The operator has adjusted the linkage.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Present perfect tense is not an approved form.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The technician is adjusting the valve.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Progressive tense is not an approved form.

name: Use only approved technical noun categories
description: When you use a word as a technical noun, it must belong to one of the approved technical noun categories. These categories include official parts, vehicles, tools, materials, and others. Your company or project must approve the word for its category.
specText: Use a word as a technical noun only if it belongs to an approved technical noun category.

compliantExamples.text: bolt, cable, clip, conductor, contact, engine, screw, switch (category 1 — official parts)
aircraft, cockpit, fuselage, helicopter, wing (category 2 — vehicles or machines)

name: Use unapproved words only as technical nouns
description: If a word is not in the STE dictionary, you can use it only as a technical noun. You cannot use it as a verb, adjective, or in any other part of speech. The technical noun must be approved by your company, industry, or subject field.
specText: If a word is not in the dictionary, you can use it only as a technical noun.

compliantExamples.text: Do the backup of the computer at regular intervals. ('Backup' is a technical noun, category 19.)
The base of the triangle is 5 cm. ('Base' is a technical noun, category 7.)

nonCompliantExamples.text: The ECU interfaces with the sensor.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Interface' is approved only as a technical noun; it must not be used as a verb. Write 'The ECU connects to the sensor' or 'The ECU communicates with the sensor'.

name: Do not use technical nouns as verbs
description: A word that is approved as a technical noun must not be used as a verb (unless the same word is also an approved technical verb or dictionary verb). Use a different sentence construction with the technical noun.
specText: Do not use a technical noun as a verb.

compliantExamples.text: Apply oil to the steel surfaces.
If you think that snow will fall, make sure that the vehicle is in the applicable configuration.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The fault impacts the system performance.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Impact' is a technical noun; do not use it as a verb. Write 'The fault affects the system performance'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: This condition impacts the fuel flow.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Impact' is a technical noun; do not use it as a verb. Write 'This condition affects the fuel flow'.

name: Use technical nouns approved in your industry or subject field
description: Some technical nouns are not in the STE dictionary but are approved in your company, industry, or subject field. You can use these words as technical nouns if they are approved in the relevant context.
specText: You can use technical nouns that are approved in your company, industry, or subject field.

compliantExamples.text: The front panel of the phone has a touchscreen and a home button. ('Touchscreen' and 'home button' are approved technical nouns in the consumer electronics industry.)

name: Select short and easy-to-understand technical nouns
description: When you select a technical noun, choose a word that is short and easy for your reader to understand. Add one or two adjectives if needed to make the noun clearer, but do not use unnecessarily long or complex technical noun groups.
specText: Select technical nouns that are short and easy to understand.

compliantExamples.text: Remove the four screws (10) that attach the flange (15) to the cover (20).

nonCompliantExamples.text: Remove the four stainless steel pan head machine screws (10) that attach the metallic machined flange (15) to the front housing cover (20).
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Unnecessarily complex noun groups; use shorter, simpler technical nouns.

name: Do not use regional, slang, or jargon as technical nouns
description: Do not use regional expressions, slang, or jargon as technical nouns. These words are not clear to all readers. Use standard technical nouns that are understood internationally.
specText: Do not use regional expressions, slang, or jargon as technical nouns.

compliantExamples.text: During logging operations, attach a cable to the heavy machinery to hold the logs in their position.
Remove your tools and equipment from the work area.

nonCompliantExamples.text: During logging operations, attach a choker to the heavy machinery.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Choker' is a regional term; use 'cable'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Remove your gear from the work area.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Gear' is jargon; use 'tools and equipment'.

name: Do not use different technical nouns for the same item
description: Use the same technical noun consistently throughout a document to refer to the same item. Do not alternate between two or more different terms for the same part or concept.
specText: Use the same technical noun each time you refer to the same item.

compliantExamples.text: 1. Make sure that the actuator is in the open position. 2. Do the operational test of the actuator. 3. Disconnect the actuator from the test rig.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Inspect the pump assembly. Examine the seal for wear.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Inspect' and 'Examine' are synonyms; use one term consistently throughout the document (ASD-STE100 Rule 1.11).

name: Use only approved technical verb categories
description: When you use a word as a technical verb, it must belong to one of the approved technical verb categories. Use technical verbs only when they are necessary and correct in context. Prefer approved dictionary verbs where possible.
specText: Use a word as a technical verb only if it belongs to an approved technical verb category.

compliantExamples.text: Ream the hole until it has a diameter of 8.00 +/- 0.003 mm.
Put clamps on the cable to hold it in position.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Machine the hole until it has a diameter of 8.00 mm.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Machine' is not an approved technical verb in this context.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Grease the fasteners.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Grease' is a technical noun; do not use it as a technical verb.

name: Do not use technical verbs as nouns
description: A word that is approved as a technical verb must not be used as a noun (unless the same word is also approved as a technical noun or dictionary noun). Rewrite the sentence so that the technical verb is used as a verb.
specText: Do not use a technical verb as a noun.

compliantExamples.text: Ream the hole to a 0.20-inch dimension.
Lubricate the reamed hole. ('Reamed' is the past participle of technical verb 'ream', used as an adjective.)

nonCompliantExamples.text: Give the hole a 0.20-inch ream.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Ream' is a technical verb; do not use it as a noun. Write: 'Ream the hole to 0.20 inch'.

name: Use American English spelling
description: Use American English spelling unless a different spelling is specified by your company or client. For example, write 'color' not 'colour', 'center' not 'centre', 'realize' not 'realise'.
specText: Use American English spelling unless another directive applies.

compliantExamples.text: color, center, realize, organize, behavior, favor

nonCompliantExamples.text: colour, centre, realise, organise, behaviour, favour
nonCompliantExamples.reason: British English spelling; use American English spelling.

name: Multi-word noun: three words maximum
description: A technical noun that consists of more than one word (a multi-word noun) must have a maximum of three words. If you need more than three words, rewrite the noun using prepositions or hyphens, or give it a shorter form.
specText: A multi-word noun must have three words or fewer.

compliantExamples.text: Calibration of the resistance of the runway light connection. (1 word, 1 word, and 3 words)
Install the terminal tags on the forward overheat thermocouple of the turbine. (2 words and 3 words)

nonCompliantExamples.text: Inspect the connection resistance indicator.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Four-word noun cluster (connection resistance indicator); restructure using a preposition, e.g. "indicator for connection resistance".

nonCompliantExamples.text: Check the indicator tolerance measurement.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Four-word noun cluster (indicator tolerance measurement); restructure, e.g. "measurement of indicator tolerance".

name: Write long technical nouns in full, then shorten with hyphens or abbreviation
description: When a technical noun has more than three words, write it in full the first time. Then you can use a shorter form, hyphens between words used as one unit, or an approved abbreviation. This makes the technical noun clear to the reader.
specText: When a technical noun has more than three words, write it in full the first time, then use a shorter form.

compliantExamples.text: Constant Speed Drive (CSD) — write in full first, then use 'CSD'.
Use hyphens between words used as a unit: air-conditioned compartment.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Check the actuator indicator.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Three-word noun cluster; clarify the relationship with a preposition: write 'indicator for the actuator'.

name: Use only the verb forms given in the dictionary
description: For each verb in the STE dictionary, the dictionary lists which forms are approved (e.g. infinitive, imperative, simple present, simple past, future). Use only those forms. Do not use verb forms that are not given in the dictionary entry.
specText: Use only the verb forms that the dictionary gives.

compliantExamples.text: REMOVE (v): (To) Remove / Remove / Remove(s) / Removed / Removed (past participle as adjective)

nonCompliantExamples.text: The technician has installed the component.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Present perfect tense (has installed) is not an approved verb form; use simple past: "The technician installed the component."

nonCompliantExamples.text: The operator was checking the pressure.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Progressive tense (was checking) is not an approved verb form; use simple past: "The operator checked the pressure."

name: Use only the approved verb forms and tenses
description: Only these verb forms and tenses are approved: infinitive, imperative, simple present, simple past, future ('will + verb'). Do not use the present perfect, past perfect, or progressive (continuous) tenses.
specText: Use only the approved tenses: infinitive, imperative, simple present, simple past, and future.

compliantExamples.text: Adjust + object / You adjust / It adjusts / You adjusted / It adjusted / You will adjust
Give + object / You give / It gives / You gave / It gave / You will give

nonCompliantExamples.text: The operator has adjusted the linkage.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Present perfect tense is not approved.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The operator had adjusted the linkage.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Past perfect tense is not approved.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The operator is adjusting the linkage.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Progressive tense is not approved.

name: Use the past participle only as an adjective
description: You can use the past participle form of an approved verb as an adjective, either before a noun or after the verb 'to be'. Do not use the past participle as a verb form in a compound tense.
specText: You can use the past participle of an approved verb only as an adjective.

compliantExamples.text: Examine all parts of the disassembled unit for damage. ('Disassembled' is an adjective before the noun 'unit'.)
When the unit is fully disassembled, clean all the parts. ('Disassembled' is an adjective after the verb 'to be'.)

name: Do not use auxiliary verbs for complex verb constructions
description: Do not use the past participle as a verb together with an auxiliary verb (e.g. have/has, is/are to be, can be, must be). These constructions create unapproved tenses and passive voice constructions. Use simple tenses and the active voice instead.
specText: Do not use auxiliary verbs to make complex verb constructions.

compliantExamples.text: The operator adjusted the linkage. (Simple past, approved.)
Before you install the cushion, install the seat.
You can adjust the volume control.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The operator should check the linkage.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Should' is a prohibited auxiliary; use 'must' for obligation.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The seat is to be installed before you install the cushion.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Complex passive construction; use active voice.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The volume control can be adjusted.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Passive; rewrite in active voice.

name: Use the -ing form only as a technical noun or modifier in a technical noun
description: Do not use the -ing form of a verb in a gerund construction (as a noun or in a clause). You can use the -ing form only when it is part of an approved technical noun or as a modifier in a technical noun group.
specText: Use the -ing form of a verb only as a technical noun or as a modifier in a technical noun.

compliantExamples.text: When you do this procedure, obey all the safety precautions.
Before you use dangerous materials, obey these precautions.

nonCompliantExamples.text: After installing the filter, bleed the hydraulic system.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Gerund after preposition 'after'; write 'After you install the filter, bleed the hydraulic system'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Cleaning the unit is required before storage.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Gerund as sentence subject; write 'Clean the unit before you store it'.

name: Use the active voice
description: Write sentences in the active voice. The subject of the sentence performs the action. You can use the passive voice in descriptive writing only when the agent is unknown or unimportant. In procedural writing, use the imperative form.
specText: Use the active voice. Use the passive voice in descriptive writing only when the agent is unknown.

compliantExamples.text: A switching relay connects the circuits. (Active)
The computer calculates the energy consumption from these values. (Active)
Continue the test. (Active imperative)

nonCompliantExamples.text: The circuits are connected by a switching relay. (Passive)
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Agent is known; use active voice.

nonCompliantExamples.text: These values are used by the computer to calculate the energy consumption. (Passive)
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Agent is known; use active voice.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The test can be continued by the operator. (Passive)
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Use imperative: 'Continue the test'.

name: Use an approved verb to describe an action
description: Use an approved verb (from the dictionary) to describe an action. Do not replace an approved verb with a noun-based construction (nominalization) such as 'make a decision' instead of 'decide', or 'perform an inspection' instead of 'inspect'.
specText: Use an approved verb to describe an action. Do not replace a verb with a noun construction.

compliantExamples.text: Decide on the best method.
Inspect the component.
Verify the torque value.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Make a decision on the best method.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Nominalization; use 'decide'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Perform an inspection of the component.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Nominalization; use 'inspect'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Do a verification of the torque value.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Nominalization; use 'verify'.

name: Write short and clear sentences
description: Write sentences that are short and easy to understand. Each sentence must have one main topic. If a sentence contains more than one topic, write separate sentences for each topic.
specText: Write short and clear sentences. Write one topic per sentence.

compliantExamples.text: 1. Remove the cover assembly (9) as follows: A. Remove the four screws (10). B. Remove the cover (11) from the housing (12). C. Remove and discard the preformed packing (13).
The side stay assembly has two folding toggles. The folding toggles are attached together with hinges. These folding toggles are also attached between the main gear strut and the side stay bracket.

nonCompliantExamples.text: It is important to check the oil level.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Impersonal abstract construction; write 'Check the oil level' as a direct imperative instruction.

nonCompliantExamples.text: No leaks are permitted.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Abstract passive negative that hides responsibility; write 'Make sure that there are no leaks'.

name: Do not omit words or use contractions
description: Write every word that the reader needs to understand the sentence. Do not omit verbs, subjects, or articles. Do not use contractions (e.g. 'don't', 'can't', 'it's'); write the full forms instead.
specText: Do not omit words. Do not use contractions.

compliantExamples.text: Set the rotary switch to INPUT.
If shims are installed, remove them.
Cracks can have a maximum length of five inches.

nonCompliantExamples.text: And connect the test unit.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Sentence starts with conjunction 'And'; begin with the imperative verb instead.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Use the correct tool & check the result.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Symbol '&' is not approved; write 'and'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Don't use that part.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Contraction; write 'Do not'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The duct efficiency is 80%.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Symbol '%' is not approved; write 'percent'.

name: Use a vertical list for complex information
description: When you have complex texts with parallel items (parts, work steps, conditions), use a vertical list. Vertical lists are easier to read than long sentences with multiple elements. Use letters or numbers to identify each item.
specText: Use a vertical list when the text is complex and has parallel items.

compliantExamples.text: The wheel assembly has these parts: - The tire - The tube - The spokes - The spoke fittings - The valve - The hub.
If the Ram Air Turbine (RAT) is retracted: (a) Remove the tag. (b) Open the isolating valves. (c) Slowly and fully extend the RAT.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The wheel assembly comprises the tire, the tube, the spokes, the spoke fittings, the valve, and the hub.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Long inline list; use a vertical list.

nonCompliantExamples.text: If the RAT is retracted, remove the tag, open the isolating valves and, ensuring that there is no possibility of fouling, slowly extend the RAT to its full stroke.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Multiple actions in one sentence; use a vertical list.

name: Use connecting words and phrases for related sentences
description: Use approved connecting words and phrases (e.g. 'and', 'but', 'thus', 'if', 'this', 'these') to show the relationship between sentences and paragraphs. Connecting words help the reader follow the logic of the text.
specText: Use connecting words and phrases to show the relationship between sentences.

compliantExamples.text: The localizer course aligns with the centerline of the runway. And the glideslope path is at a constant angle to the threshold of the runway.
If the pressure increases, it changes the electrical currents in the transmitter. Thus, the power unit supplies more current.

name: Use an article or demonstrative adjective before a noun
description: Use an article (the, a, an) or a demonstrative adjective (this, that, these, those) before a noun or multi-word noun when applicable. Omitting articles can cause ambiguity and makes the text harder to read.
specText: Use an article or demonstrative adjective before a noun or multi-word noun when applicable.

compliantExamples.text: Remove the cover.
Install a new O-ring.
Use these fasteners.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Remove cover.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Article 'the' omitted before noun; write 'Remove the cover'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Install O-ring.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Article 'an' omitted before noun; write 'Install an O-ring'.

name: Maximum 20 words per instructional sentence
description: An instructional sentence must not have more than 20 words. Count all words in the sentence (see Section 8 for word-count rules). If a sentence is too long, divide it into shorter sentences or use a vertical list.
specText: An instructional sentence must have no more than 20 words.

compliantExamples.text: Install the three auxiliary screws (2) in the flange of the motor assembly (9). [9 words]
CAUTION: WHEN YOU REMOVE THE SHROUD (26), BE CAREFUL NOT TO CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE SURFACE OF THE FLANGE ASSEMBLY (22). [20 words]

nonCompliantExamples.text: Put preservation oil into the unit through the vent hole until the oil level is approximately 6 mm (0.24 inches) below the surface of the flange cover.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: More than 20 words; divide into two sentences.

name: Write only one instruction per sentence
description: Each instructional sentence must give only one instruction (one action). If two actions must occur at the same time, you can write both in one sentence. If the actions occur at different times, write separate sentences.
specText: Write only one instruction per sentence, unless two actions must occur at the same time.

compliantExamples.text: (1) Set the TEST switch to the middle position. (2) Make sure that all the switches on the control panel are OFF.
Hold the panel in its open position and install the fastener. (Two simultaneous actions — permitted.)

nonCompliantExamples.text: Set the TEST switch to the middle position and release the SHORT-CIRCUIT TEST switch.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Two separate actions in one sentence; write as two steps.

name: Write instructions in the imperative form
description: Write each instruction as an imperative (command). The imperative form gives a clear, direct instruction to the reader. Do not use 'must', 'shall', or passive constructions for instructions unless it is necessary for safety emphasis.
specText: Write each instruction in the imperative form.

compliantExamples.text: Set the switch to ON.
Remove the four bolts.
Increase the pressure to 60 psi.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The test can be continued.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Not imperative; write 'Continue the test'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Oil and grease must be removed with a degreasing agent.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Modal-passive construction, not imperative; write 'Remove oil and grease with a degreasing agent'.

name: Put the condition before the command, with a comma between them
description: When a sentence has a condition and a command, write the condition first, then put a comma after it, then write the command. This structure prevents ambiguity about which part of the sentence the adverb or modifier belongs to.
specText: Write the condition before the command. Use a comma after the condition.

compliantExamples.text: If the Constant Speed Drive (CSD) does not operate correctly, disconnect it from the gearbox.

name: Write notes only to give information
description: A NOTE must give information only, not instructions. If you need to give an instruction, use an imperative sentence or a numbered work step, not a NOTE. Do not use a NOTE to repeat a safety instruction.
specText: Use a NOTE only to give information. Do not write instructions in a NOTE.

compliantExamples.text: NOTE: The pressure reading will vary with altitude.
NOTE: This procedure applies only to units manufactured after January 2020.

nonCompliantExamples.text: NOTE: Remove the cover before you start.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: An instruction must not be in a NOTE; use a numbered step.

name: Give information gradually
description: In descriptive writing, give information to the reader in a logical, gradual way. Start with the most general or important information, then add specific details. Do not begin with specific details before you have introduced the topic.
specText: Give information gradually from the most general to the most specific.

compliantExamples.text: Instrument Landing System. The Instrument Landing System (the system) on the aircraft shows data that helps the pilot during the approach to the runway. This system shows the pilot the deviations from the localizer course and the glideslope path. The localizer course aligns with the centerline of the runway.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The hydraulic system, which controls the landing gear and was designed for 3000 psi operation, requires monthly inspection. Inspect it every month.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Specific detail packed into the first sentence before the topic is introduced; give general information first, then add detail in subsequent sentences.

name: Use key words and phrases to show logical structure
description: In descriptive writing, use key words and phrases to connect sentences and paragraphs. Repeat key words from one sentence to the next to show the reader how sentences are related and to build a logical structure.
specText: Use key words and phrases from sentence to sentence to show the logical structure.

compliantExamples.text: The Instrument Landing System (the system) on the aircraft shows data that helps the pilot. This system shows the pilot the deviations from the localizer course. (Key words 'system' and 'pilot' are repeated to link the sentences.)

name: Maximum 25 words per descriptive sentence
description: A descriptive sentence must not have more than 25 words. Count all words in the sentence (see Section 8 for word-count rules). If a sentence is too long, divide it into shorter sentences.
specText: A descriptive sentence must have no more than 25 words.

compliantExamples.text: During the approach to the runway, deviation pointers in the course indicators show the pilot in which direction the aircraft must go.
A smartphone is a cellular telephone that has an integrated computer and many other functions. It includes an operating system and an internet browser, and it can also operate software applications.

nonCompliantExamples.text: A smartphone is a cellular telephone that has an integrated computer and many other functions, such as an operating system, internet browsing as well as the ability to run software applications.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: More than 25 words; divide into two sentences.

name: Use paragraphs to show related information
description: Group related sentences into paragraphs. Each paragraph must contain sentences that are closely related to the same topic. Use a new paragraph when you change to a different topic.
specText: Use paragraphs to group related information. Start a new paragraph when the topic changes.

compliantExamples.text: 1. Lightning Strike. A. General. (1) A lightning strike can cause damage to the aircraft. The damage usually occurs at the attachment points. (2) From the attachment points, the lightning current moves...

name: Write one topic per paragraph
description: Each paragraph must have only one main topic. All sentences in the paragraph must relate to that topic. If you need to describe a different topic, start a new paragraph.
specText: Write about only one topic in each paragraph.

compliantExamples.text: The Instrument Landing System (the system) on the aircraft shows data that helps the pilot during the approach to the runway. This system shows the pilot the deviations from the localizer course and the glideslope path. The localizer course aligns with the centerline of the runway. And the glideslope path is at a constant angle to the threshold of the runway.

name: Maximum six sentences per paragraph
description: A descriptive paragraph must not have more than six sentences. If a paragraph is too long, divide it into shorter paragraphs, each with one topic.
specText: A paragraph must have no more than six sentences.

compliantExamples.text: A paragraph with no more than six sentences about the Instrument Landing System.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The hydraulic system controls all primary flight surfaces. The pump provides pressure to the actuators. The actuators move the control surfaces. The relief valve prevents overpressure. The filter removes contamination from the fluid. The reservoir stores the hydraulic fluid. The pressure gauge indicates the system pressure.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Seven sentences in one paragraph; divide into two paragraphs of six sentences or fewer.

name: Use the applicable safety word for the level of risk
description: Use the correct safety word (WARNING, CAUTION, or DANGER) for the level of risk. WARNING is for risk of injury or death. CAUTION is for risk of damage to equipment. DANGER is for immediate risk of death. Do not use WARNING when you mean CAUTION, or vice versa.
specText: Use the applicable safety word (WARNING, CAUTION, DANGER) for the level of risk.

compliantExamples.text: WARNING: BEFORE YOU FILL THE LIQUID OXYGEN SYSTEM, PUT ON A FACE MASK AND PROTECTIVE CLOTHING. LIQUID OXYGEN CAN CAUSE IRRITATION OF THE RESPIRATORY TRACT AND EYE IRRITATION.
WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT THE OXYGEN TUBES ARE FULLY CLEAN. OXYGEN AND GREASE MAKE AN EXPLOSIVE MIXTURE. AN EXPLOSION CAN CAUSE INJURY OR DEATH.

nonCompliantExamples.text: CAUTION: EXTREME CLEANLINESS OF OXYGEN TUBES IS IMPERATIVE.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Risk of explosion/death requires WARNING, not CAUTION.

name: Start a safety instruction with a clear command or condition
description: The safety instruction must start with a clear command (imperative) or a condition (if-clause). The reader must immediately understand what action to take or what situation applies. Do not start with vague or unclear language.
specText: Start each safety instruction with a clear command or condition.

compliantExamples.text: WARNING: DO NOT SWALLOW THE SOLVENT. ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT YOU KNOW THE SAFETY PRECAUTIONS AND FIRST AID INSTRUCTIONS FOR SOLVENTS. SOLVENTS ARE POISONOUS AND CAN CAUSE INJURY OR DEATH.
CAUTION: DO NOT USE BLEACH OR CLEANSERS THAT CONTAIN CHLORINE TO CLEAN THE UNIT. THESE CLEANING AGENTS CAN CAUSE CORROSION.

name: Give an explanation to show the risk or possible result
description: A safety instruction must explain the risk or possible result of not following the instruction. Do not use only a cross-reference (e.g. 'See Figure 1' or 'Refer to Section 3') without also stating the hazard or consequence.
specText: Give an explanation of the risk or possible result in the safety instruction itself.

compliantExamples.text: WARNING: DO NOT SWALLOW THE SOLVENT. SOLVENTS ARE POISONOUS AND CAN CAUSE INJURY OR DEATH. (Explains the risk.)
CAUTION: WHEN YOU ASSEMBLE THE UNIT, DO NOT LET THE PARTS FALL. IF THEY FALL, PERMANENT DAMAGE TO THE PARTS CAN OCCUR. (Explains the result.)

nonCompliantExamples.text: WARNING: DO NOT remove the safety panel while the equipment is in use.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Does not explain the risk or possible result; add a sentence stating the hazard (e.g. 'Removal can cause injury').

name: Use standard punctuation; do not use semicolons
description: Use standard punctuation marks (period, comma, colon, hyphen, parentheses). Do not use the semicolon (;). If you need a semicolon, write two separate sentences instead.
specText: Use standard punctuation. Do not use semicolons.

compliantExamples.text: (1) Examine the removed parts for damage. (2) Replace the damaged part(s).
Users cannot replace the battery. Only specialists at approved service stations can replace it.

nonCompliantExamples.text: (1) Examine the removed parts; replace the damaged ones.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Semicolon used; write as two separate sentences.

nonCompliantExamples.text: The battery is not user-replaceable; it can only be replaced by an approved service station.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Semicolon used; write as two separate sentences.

name: Use hyphens between directly related words
description: Use a hyphen (-) to connect two or more words that you use as one unit (a compound modifier or part of a technical noun). Hyphens help the reader understand which words are directly related.
specText: Use hyphens to connect directly related words that you use as one unit.

compliantExamples.text: low-altitude flight
high-pressure chamber
air-conditioned compartment
transmitter-receiver system
quick-release fastener

name: Use parentheses only for their allowed purposes
description: Use parentheses only for: (1) references to figures, tables, paragraphs; (2) numbers or letters that identify items in illustrations; (3) work-step identifiers in procedures; (4) abbreviations; (5) singular and plural forms of nouns at the same time (e.g. 'part(s)').
specText: Use parentheses only for references, identifiers, abbreviations, or the singular/plural notation.

compliantExamples.text: Remove the valve (10, Figure 1). (Reference to figure/item number)
A Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) is a flat-panel display... (Abbreviation)
Replace the damaged part(s). (Singular/plural notation)

name: Use a colon before a vertical list
description: Use a colon (:) at the end of the introductory sentence or phrase that precedes a vertical list. The introductory text must be a complete thought. Do not use a colon if the list continues the sentence grammatically without a break.
specText: Use a colon before a vertical list.

compliantExamples.text: To extinguish a possible fire, portable fire extinguishers are installed in these areas: - The cockpit - The cabin - The cabin sub-compartment - The crew rest compartment.

name: Count parenthetical text as one word
description: When you count words in a sentence, count all text in parentheses as one word, regardless of how many words it contains. This rule applies to word-count checks for rules 5.1 and 6.3.
specText: Count any text in parentheses as one word when you count words.

compliantExamples.text: Make sure that the EMER pushbutton switch is released (the EMER legend is off). [This sentence has 10 words, because the text in parentheses counts as one word.]
Remove the safety pin (10). [5 words; the identifier in parentheses counts as one word.]

name: Count numbers, units, abbreviations, and identifiers as one word each
description: When you count words in a sentence, count each number, unit of measurement, abbreviation, alphanumeric identifier, or quoted text as one word, regardless of its length or complexity.
specText: Count each number, unit, abbreviation, identifier, and quoted text as one word.

compliantExamples.text: Torque the bolt to 4.20 Nm. [4.20 counts as one word, Nm counts as one word.]
Set the switch to ON. ['ON' counts as one word.]

name: Count hyphenated words as one word
description: When you count words in a sentence, count a hyphenated compound as one word. For example, 'air-conditioned' counts as one word, and 'quick-release' counts as one word.
specText: Count a hyphenated compound as one word when you count words.

compliantExamples.text: Install the quick-release fastener. ['quick-release' counts as one word.]
Check the low-altitude flight parameters. ['low-altitude' counts as one word.]

name: Use a different sentence construction when word-for-word replacement fails
description: When you replace an unapproved word with an approved alternative, make sure the meaning of the sentence does not change. If word-for-word replacement changes the meaning, use a different sentence construction that preserves the original meaning.
specText: Use a different sentence construction if a direct word replacement changes the meaning.

compliantExamples.text: Connect the pump to the valve. Lubricate the pump before connection.
Remove the cover and the retaining clip. Discard the retaining clip.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Connect the pump to the valve. It must be lubricated first.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'It' could refer to the pump or the valve; name the referent explicitly to remove the ambiguity.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Remove the cover and the retaining clip. This can be discarded.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'This' is ambiguous — it could refer to the cover or the retaining clip; write 'Discard the retaining clip'.

name: Use each approved word correctly
description: Use each approved word only with its approved meaning and in a context where the meaning is correct. Do not use an approved word if its approved meaning does not match what you want to say in the sentence.
specText: Use each approved word correctly — in the right context and with the right meaning.

compliantExamples.text: Use (or put on) protective clothing. ('Wear' has the approved meaning 'to become damaged by friction'; use 'put on' for clothing.)
This regulation is applicable to all units. ('Extend' approved meaning is 'to increase in dimension'; do not use it here.)

nonCompliantExamples.text: Wear protective clothing.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Wear' is not approved with the meaning of 'to dress in'; use 'put on' or 'use'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Utilize the correct tool for the procedure.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Utilize' should be replaced with 'use'; it is not an approved STE word.

name: Do not use phrasal verbs
description: Do not use phrasal verbs (a verb combined with a preposition or adverb that creates a new meaning different from the approved dictionary meaning of each word). Instead, use a single approved verb with the same meaning.
specText: Do not use phrasal verbs. Use a single approved verb instead.

compliantExamples.text: After you extinguish the fire, close the valve on the fire extinguisher.
This compound can release poisonous fumes.

nonCompliantExamples.text: After you put out the fire, close the valve on the fire extinguisher.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Put out' is a phrasal verb; use 'extinguish'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: This compound can give off poisonous fumes.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: 'Give off' is a phrasal verb; use 'release'.

name: Use consistent terminology and wording
description: Use the same words and sentence structures each time you describe the same action, concept, or situation. Do not alternate between different words or sentence structures for the same meaning. Consistency helps the reader understand and remember the information.
specText: Use consistent terminology and sentence structure throughout the document.

compliantExamples.text: See Figure 1 for the valve assembly diagram.
Install the LRU in the rack. Check the LRU for damage. (Term 'LRU' capitalised consistently.)

nonCompliantExamples.text: See fig. 1 for the valve assembly diagram.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Abbreviated cross-reference; spell out and capitalise: write 'Figure 1'.

nonCompliantExamples.text: Install the LRU in the rack. Check the Lru for damage.
nonCompliantExamples.reason: Inconsistent capitalisation of the same term ('LRU' vs 'Lru'); use one form consistently throughout.
